topic: What if everyone disappeared except you?

script.text: And then, for a few days, it is the best thing that has ever happened to you.
Day two. You walk into the biggest toy store in the city and take whatever you want. Nobody stops you. There is no queue at the checkout, because there is nobody at the checkout.
On the way home, you stop at Mo's house and stick a note on his door. Gone to the mall. Come find me. Every day after that, you check. Every day, the note is still there.
Day three. Breakfast is ice cream. Lunch is ice cream. Dinner is a whole pizza from the food court, which you work out how to bake yourself. It's terrible. You eat all of it anyway.
Day four. You ride a bike down the middle of the motorway, past thousands of stopped cars, singing as loud as you can. Nobody tells you to stop.

Day five. You move into the penthouse at the top of the fanciest hotel in the city. The bed is bigger than your bedroom. There's a hot tub on the balcony. You fall asleep in a bathrobe, watching the sun set over a city that belongs only to you.
That night you watch a film alone in the biggest cinema in town, in the best seat, with a bucket of popcorn the size of a bin. It takes you an hour to work out the projector.
Day six. You go to school, just to sit in the teacher's chair. On the board, in giant letters, you write: no homework, forever.
Then you climb up onto the roof, and you scream as loud as you can, just because you can. And for the first time, something answers. All across the city, thousands of dogs start barking back.
It's funny. For about a second. Then you realise the dogs are the loudest thing left. And that the city is about to start falling apart.

shots.note: walking out with a trolley of toys
asleep in a bathrobe at sunset
popcorn the size of a bin
you scream on the school roof
the city at dusk, you small
